reviewed_types.syntax: # [doc = " The instrument governing a document, chosen from its envelope and the"] # [doc = " held state alone."] # [doc = ""] # [doc = " ```"] # [doc = " use pn_interchange::{"] # [doc = "     dispatch, Coordinate, Envelope, Instrument, NamespaceLabel, Registry, Theory, Version,"] # [doc = " };"] # [doc = ""] # [doc = " let label = NamespaceLabel::parse(\"com.example\").expect(\"a label\");"] # [doc = " let theory = Theory::parse(r#\"e = {0 => \"com.example\", 1 => [1, 0, uint], 2 => tstr}\"#)"] # [doc = "     .expect(\"an assignable theory\");"] # [doc = " let mut registry = Registry::new();"] # [doc = " registry"] # [doc = "     .acquire(Coordinate::new(label.clone(), 1, 0), theory)"] # [doc = "     .expect(\"the first minor\");"] # [doc = ""] # [doc = " let envelope = Envelope::new(label, Version::new(1, 0, 3));"] # [doc = " assert!(matches!("] # [doc = "     dispatch(&registry, &envelope),"] # [doc = "     Instrument::Strict { minor: 0, .. }"] # [doc = " ));"] # [doc = " ```"] # [derive (Debug)] pub enum Instrument < 'r > { # [doc = " The stamp is held: the strict verdict is `d ⊨ R(ℓ, M, m)`."] Strict { # [doc = " The stamped minor, which is the held minor governing."] minor : u64 , # [doc = " The theory held there."] theory : & 'r Theory , } , # [doc = " The stamp outruns the ceiling: the tolerant verdict is"] # [doc = " `d ⊨ Open(R(ℓ, M, m₁))`."] Tolerant { # [doc = " The reader's floor: the ceiling of that major."] floor : u64 , # [doc = " The companion of the theory held at the floor."] companion : & 'r OpenTheory , } , # [doc = " No instrument: the document is rejected whole."] Refused (RejectionCause) , }

# [doc = " Why no instrument governs."] # [doc = ""] # [doc = " ```"] # [doc = " use pn_interchange::{"] # [doc = "     dispatch, Envelope, Instrument, NamespaceLabel, RejectionCause, Registry, Version,"] # [doc = " };"] # [doc = ""] # [doc = " let label = NamespaceLabel::parse(\"com.example\").expect(\"a label\");"] # [doc = " let envelope = Envelope::new(label, Version::new(4, 0, 0));"] # [doc = " assert!(matches!("] # [doc = "     dispatch(&Registry::new(), &envelope),"] # [doc = "     Instrument::Refused(RejectionCause::UnheldMajor)"] # [doc = " ));"] # [doc = " ```"] # [derive (Copy , Clone , Debug , PartialEq , Eq)] # [non_exhaustive] pub enum RejectionCause { # [doc = " No minor of this major is held."] UnheldMajor , # [doc = " The stamp lies at or below the ceiling and was never assigned: a"] # [doc = " checkably false claim."] UnassignedStamp { # [doc = " The reader's ceiling of that major."] ceiling : u64 , } , }

# [doc = " The disposition of a document at a reader."] # [doc = ""] # [doc = " ```"] # [doc = " use pn_interchange::{NamespaceLabel, Rejection, Registry, Verdict};"] # [doc = ""] # [doc = " let verdict = Verdict::AcceptedStrictly { minor: 2 };"] # [doc = " assert!(verdict.is_accepted());"] # [doc = " assert!(!Verdict::Rejected(Rejection::UnheldMajor { major: 1 }).is_accepted());"] # [doc = " ```"] # [derive (Clone , Debug , PartialEq , Eq)] # [non_exhaustive] pub enum Verdict { # [doc = " The document satisfies the theory held at its stamp."] AcceptedStrictly { # [doc = " The stamped minor, which the reader holds."] minor : u64 , } , # [doc = " The stamp outruns the reader, and the document satisfies the"] # [doc = " companion of the reader's floor."] AcceptedTolerantly { # [doc = " The reader's floor: its ceiling of that major."] floor : u64 , } , # [doc = " The document is rejected, and here is why."] Rejected (Rejection) , }

# [doc = " Why a document was rejected."] # [doc = ""] # [doc = " The first two arms are facts about the reader's state rather than about"] # [doc = " the document: a state that grows over what the owner assigned turns"] # [doc = " them toward acceptance. The third is a fact about the document, under"] # [doc = " the instrument named."] # [doc = ""] # [doc = " ```"] # [doc = " use pn_interchange::{Rejection, Under};"] # [doc = ""] # [doc = " let rejection = Rejection::UnassignedStamp { minor: 3, ceiling: 5 };"] # [doc = " assert!(matches!(rejection, Rejection::UnassignedStamp { minor: 3, .. }));"] # [doc = " assert_eq!(Under::Strict { minor: 1 }, Under::Strict { minor: 1 });"] # [doc = " ```"] # [derive (Clone , Debug , PartialEq , Eq)] # [non_exhaustive] pub enum Rejection { # [doc = " The reader holds no minor of this major."] UnheldMajor { # [doc = " The major the document stamps."] major : u64 , } , # [doc = " The stamp lies at or below the ceiling and was never assigned."] UnassignedStamp { # [doc = " The minor the document stamps."] minor : u64 , # [doc = " The reader's ceiling of that major, which the stamp does not"] # [doc = " outrun."] ceiling : u64 , } , # [doc = " The instrument governed, and the document did not satisfy it."] Unsatisfied { # [doc = " Which instrument judged."] under : Under , # [doc = " Every way the document failed it, in ascending key order."] mismatches : Vec < Mismatch > , } , }

# [doc = " Which instrument a judgment ran under."] # [doc = ""] # [doc = " ```"] # [doc = " use pn_interchange::Under;"] # [doc = ""] # [doc = " assert_ne!(Under::Strict { minor: 1 }, Under::Tolerant { floor: 1 });"] # [doc = " ```"] # [derive (Copy , Clone , Debug , PartialEq , Eq)] pub enum Under { # [doc = " The theory held at the document's stamp."] Strict { # [doc = " The stamped minor."] minor : u64 , } , # [doc = " The open companion of the reader's floor."] Tolerant { # [doc = " The floor whose companion judged."] floor : u64 , } , }

# [doc = " A whole CDDL source: `cddl = S 1*(rule S)`."] # [doc = ""] # [doc = " At least one rule, because the ABNF says `1*`."] # [derive (Clone , Debug)] # [allow (dead_code)] pub (crate) struct Cddl { # [doc = " The rules, in the order they were written. The first is the root."] pub (crate) rules : Vec < Rule > , # [doc = " The whole source."] pub (crate) span : Span , }

# [doc = " One rule: `rule = typename [genericparm] S assignt S type`"] # [doc = " or `groupname [genericparm] S assigng S grpent`."] # [derive (Clone , Debug)] pub (crate) struct Rule { # [doc = " The type name or group name being defined."] pub (crate) name : Name , # [doc = " `genericparm`, when the rule is generic."] pub (crate) params : Option < GenericParams > , # [doc = " Which assignment operator was written."] pub (crate) assign : Assign , # [doc = " What the rule assigns."] pub (crate) body : RuleBody , # [doc = " The whole rule."] pub (crate) span : Span , }

# [doc = " The assignment operator, kept because the two augmenting forms mean"] # [doc = " something the plain form does not."] # [doc = ""] # [doc = " `assignt = \"=\" / \"/=\"` and `assigng = \"=\" / \"//=\"`: `=` defines,"] # [doc = " `/=` adds a type choice to an existing name, `//=` adds a group choice."] # [doc = " The augmenting forms are what makes the socket/plug convention of"] # [doc = " RFC 8610 Section 3.9 work."] # [derive (Copy , Clone , Debug , PartialEq , Eq)] pub (crate) enum Assign { # [doc = " `=`"] Plain , # [doc = " `/=`, adding an alternative to a type choice."] TypeChoice , # [doc = " `//=`, adding an alternative to a group choice."] GroupChoice , }

# [doc = " What a rule assigns: a type, or a group entry."] # [doc = ""] # [doc = " The two rule alternatives of the ABNF are told apart by what follows"] # [doc = " the assignment, not by the name in front of it — `typename` and"] # [doc = " `groupname` are both `id`. With `=` either is possible, and the parser"] # [doc = " resolves it as the ordered choice does: a type if the text is one, a"] # [doc = " group entry otherwise."] # [derive (Clone , Debug)] pub (crate) enum RuleBody { # [doc = " A type rule."] Type (Type) , # [doc = " A group rule, whose body is one `grpent`."] # [doc = ""] # [doc = " Boxed: a group entry carries an occurrence indicator and a member"] # [doc = " key that a type never has, and type rules are the common case."] Group (Box < GroupEntry >) , }

# [doc = " An `id` as it appears in the source: a type name, group name, bareword,"] # [doc = " control-operator name, or generic parameter."] # [derive (Clone , Debug)] pub (crate) struct Name { # [doc = " The identifier, byte for byte."] pub (crate) text : String , # [doc = " Where it was written."] pub (crate) span : Span , }

# [doc = " `genericparm = \"<\" S id S *(\",\" S id S ) \">\"`."] # [derive (Clone , Debug)] # [allow (dead_code)] pub (crate) struct GenericParams { # [doc = " The parameter names, in order. Never empty: the ABNF requires one."] pub (crate) names : Vec < Name > , # [doc = " From `<` to `>`."] pub (crate) span : Span , }

# [doc = " `genericarg = \"<\" S type1 S *(\",\" S type1 S ) \">\"`."] # [derive (Clone , Debug)] # [allow (dead_code)] pub (crate) struct GenericArgs { # [doc = " The arguments, in order. Never empty: the ABNF requires one."] # [doc = ""] # [doc = " The elements are `type1` and not `type`, so an argument cannot be a"] # [doc = " bare type choice; `<a / b>` is not generic-argument syntax."] pub (crate) args : Vec < Type1 > , # [doc = " From `<` to `>`."] pub (crate) span : Span , }

# [doc = " `type = type1 *(S \"/\" S type1)`: a type choice."] # [derive (Clone , Debug)] pub (crate) struct Type { # [doc = " The alternatives, in order. Never empty."] pub (crate) choices : Vec < Type1 > , # [doc = " The whole choice."] pub (crate) span : Span , }

# [doc = " `type1 = type2 [S (rangeop / ctlop) S type2]`."] # [doc = ""] # [doc = " One operation at most: ranges and control operators do not chain, so"] # [doc = " `1 .. 2 .. 3` is not CDDL."] # [derive (Clone , Debug)] pub (crate) struct Type1 { # [doc = " The left-hand type."] pub (crate) target : Type2 , # [doc = " The operator and its right-hand type, when one was written."] pub (crate) operation : Option < Operation > , # [doc = " The whole `type1`."] pub (crate) span : Span , }

# [doc = " The optional half of a `type1`."] # [derive (Clone , Debug)] # [allow (dead_code)] pub (crate) struct Operation { # [doc = " Which operator."] pub (crate) operator : Operator , # [doc = " The right-hand type."] pub (crate) operand : Type2 , # [doc = " From the operator to the end of the operand."] pub (crate) span : Span , }

# [doc = " `rangeop = \"...\" / \"..\"` and `ctlop = \".\" id`."] # [derive (Clone , Debug)] pub (crate) enum Operator { # [doc = " `..`, a range including its upper bound."] RangeInclusive , # [doc = " `...`, a range excluding its upper bound."] RangeExclusive , # [doc = " `.name`, a control operator."] # [doc = ""] # [doc = " The name is kept as a name and nothing more. Which names this crate"] # [doc = " evaluates, and which it refuses, is settled at a later stage"] # [doc = " (´[ROOT-dec:xchg:evaluable-subset]´); the parser admits every"] # [doc = " name the grammar admits, including names no implementation defines."] Control (Name) , }

# [doc = " One alternative of `type2`."] # [derive (Clone , Debug)] pub (crate) struct Type2 { # [doc = " Which alternative."] pub (crate) kind : Type2Kind , # [doc = " Where it was written."] pub (crate) span : Span , }

# [doc = " The ten alternatives of `type2`."] # [derive (Clone , Debug)] pub (crate) enum Type2Kind { # [doc = " `value`: a literal."] Value (Value) , # [doc = " `typename [genericarg]`: a reference to a type rule."] Typename { # [doc = " The referenced name."] name : Name , # [doc = " Generic arguments, when the reference instantiates them."] args : Option < GenericArgs > , } , # [doc = " `\"(\" S type S \")\"`: a parenthesized type."] # [doc = ""] # [doc = " Kept as its own node rather than unwrapped, because dropping the"] # [doc = " parentheses would change how the printed form reparses around a"] # [doc = " range or control operator."] Parenthesized (Box < Type >) , # [doc = " `\"{\" S group S \"}\"`: a map."] Map (Group) , # [doc = " `\"[\" S group S \"]\"`: an array."] Array (Group) , # [doc = " `\"~\" S typename [genericarg]`: unwrapping a tag or a wrapped group."] Unwrap { # [doc = " The name being unwrapped."] name : Name , # [doc = " Generic arguments, when the reference instantiates them."] args : Option < GenericArgs > , } , # [doc = " `\"&\" S \"(\" S group S \")\"`: the enumeration of an inline group."] EnumInline (Box < Group >) , # [doc = " `\"&\" S groupname [genericarg]`: the enumeration of a named group."] EnumGroup { # [doc = " The referenced group name."] name : Name , # [doc = " Generic arguments, when the reference instantiates them."] args : Option < GenericArgs > , } , # [doc = " `\"#\" \"6\" [\".\" uint] \"(\" S type S \")\"`: a tagged type."] Tagged { # [doc = " The tag number, absent for `#6(...)`, which tags with any"] # [doc = " number."] number : Option < Uint > , # [doc = " The type inside the tag."] inner : Box < Type > , } , # [doc = " `\"#\" DIGIT [\".\" uint]`: a major type, optionally with additional"] # [doc = " information."] Representation { # [doc = " The major type, 0 through 9 as the grammar's `DIGIT` allows."] # [doc = ""] # [doc = " CBOR defines only 0 through 7; the grammar admits 8 and 9, and"] # [doc = " the parser admits what the grammar admits."] major : u8 , # [doc = " The additional information, when one was written."] ai : Option < Uint > , } , # [doc = " `\"#\"`: any data item."] Any , }

# [doc = " An unsigned integer literal used as a number rather than as a value:"] # [doc = " a tag number, an additional information, or an occurrence bound."] # [doc = ""] # [doc = " Kept as written, so that `#6.0x18` prints back as `#6.0x18`."] # [derive (Clone , Debug)] # [allow (dead_code)] pub (crate) struct Uint { # [doc = " The digits, byte for byte, in whatever base they were written."] pub (crate) text : String , # [doc = " Where they were written."] pub (crate) span : Span , }

# [doc = " `group = grpchoice *(S \"//\" S grpchoice)`."] # [derive (Clone , Debug)] pub (crate) struct Group { # [doc = " The choices, in order. Never empty — a group with no `//` has one"] # [doc = " choice, which may itself have no entries."] pub (crate) choices : Vec < GroupChoice > , # [doc = " The whole group."] pub (crate) span : Span , }

# [doc = " `grpchoice = *(grpent optcom)`."] # [derive (Clone , Debug)] # [allow (dead_code)] pub (crate) struct GroupChoice { # [doc = " The entries, in order. May be empty: `{}` and `[]` are groups with"] # [doc = " one empty choice."] pub (crate) entries : Vec < GroupEntry > , # [doc = " The whole choice."] pub (crate) span : Span , }

# [doc = " One `grpent`."] # [derive (Clone , Debug)] pub (crate) struct GroupEntry { # [doc = " `[occur S]`."] pub (crate) occur : Option < Occur > , # [doc = " Which `grpent` alternative."] pub (crate) kind : GroupEntryKind , # [doc = " The whole entry, occurrence indicator included."] pub (crate) span : Span , }

# [doc = " The alternatives of `grpent`."] # [doc = ""] # [doc = " The ABNF lists three. The second, `[occur S] groupname [genericarg]`,"] # [doc = " carries the RFC's own comment \"preempted by above\": a bare group name"] # [doc = " is already `[occur S] [memberkey S] type` with no member key and a type"] # [doc = " that is a `typename`. It is therefore not a separate variant here —"] # [doc = " representing it separately would give one piece of source two trees."] # [derive (Clone , Debug)] pub (crate) enum GroupEntryKind { # [doc = " `[occur S] [memberkey S] type`."] Member { # [doc = " The member key, absent in an array or a bare group reference."] key : Option < MemberKey > , # [doc = " The type of the member."] value : Type , } , # [doc = " `[occur S] \"(\" S group S \")\"`: a parenthesized inline group."] Inline (Group) , }

# [doc = " `occur = [uint] \"*\" [uint] / \"+\" / \"?\"`."] # [derive (Clone , Debug)] pub (crate) struct Occur { # [doc = " Which form."] pub (crate) kind : OccurKind , # [doc = " Where it was written."] pub (crate) span : Span , }

# [doc = " The three forms of `occur`."] # [derive (Clone , Debug)] pub (crate) enum OccurKind { # [doc = " `[uint] \"*\" [uint]`: bounded below, above, both, or neither."] # [doc = ""] # [doc = " A bare `*` is this variant with both bounds absent. The ABNF admits"] # [doc = " no space anywhere inside the production, so `2 * 3` is not one"] # [doc = " occurrence indicator."] Bounded { # [doc = " The lower bound, when written."] min : Option < Uint > , # [doc = " The upper bound, when written."] max : Option < Uint > , } , # [doc = " `+`: one or more."] OneOrMore , # [doc = " `?`: zero or one."] Optional , }

# [doc = " `memberkey`."] # [derive (Clone , Debug)] pub (crate) struct MemberKey { # [doc = " Which form."] pub (crate) kind : MemberKeyKind , # [doc = " From the start of the key through its `=>` or `:`."] pub (crate) span : Span , }

# [doc = " The three forms of `memberkey`."] # [doc = ""] # [doc = " All three are distinct in the tree even where two would describe the"] # [doc = " same key, because they do not mean the same thing: `a: 1` keys on the"] # [doc = " *text string* \"a\", while `a => 1` keys on whatever the type `a`"] # [doc = " denotes."] # [derive (Clone , Debug)] pub (crate) enum MemberKeyKind { # [doc = " `type1 S [\"^\" S] \"=>\"`: a key given as a type."] Type { # [doc = " The key type."] # [doc = ""] # [doc = " Boxed: a `type1` is the deepest node of the grammar, and the"] # [doc = " other two key forms are a name and a literal."] key : Box < Type1 > , # [doc = " Whether the cut marker `^` was written."] # [doc = ""] # [doc = " A cut makes a failure to match the member's *value* a failure"] # [doc = " of the whole map, rather than a reason to try the next entry."] cut : bool , } , # [doc = " `bareword S \":\"`: a key given as a name, denoting that text string."] # [doc = ""] # [doc = " The colon form carries an implicit cut, which is why it is not the"] # [doc = " same node as a `Type` key that happens to hold a text literal."] Bareword (Name) , # [doc = " `value S \":\"`: a key given as a literal."] Value (Value) , }

# [doc = " `value = number / text / bytes`."] # [derive (Clone , Debug)] pub (crate) struct Value { # [doc = " Which kind of literal."] pub (crate) kind : ValueKind , # [doc = " Where it was written."] pub (crate) span : Span , }

# [doc = " The three kinds of literal."] # [derive (Clone , Debug)] pub (crate) enum ValueKind { # [doc = " A numeric literal, kept as written."] Number (NumberToken) , # [doc = " A text literal: the characters between the quotes, escapes intact."] # [doc = ""] # [doc = " Escapes are not resolved here. `SESC` admits any printable"] # [doc = " character after the backslash, so what an escape *denotes* is a"] # [doc = " separate question from whether it is well formed, and the parser"] # [doc = " answers only the second."] Text (String) , # [doc = " A byte-string literal: the characters between the quotes, escapes"] # [doc = " intact, with the qualifier that says how to read them."] Bytes { # [doc = " `h`, `b64`, or nothing."] qual : ByteQual , # [doc = " The characters between the quotes, byte for byte."] raw : String , } , }

# [doc = " The open companion of an assigned theory: the minor position freed to"] # [doc = " `uint`, the closure replaced by the base theory's wildcard, each"] # [doc = " enumerated content key cut, nothing else moved."] # [doc = ""] # [doc = " Derived, never assigned. That this is a type distinct from"] # [doc = " [`Theory`] is how the crate carries \"Open(S) is derived, never assigned"] # [doc = " — it enters no registry\": the clause is a signature that does not"] # [doc = " typecheck rather than a runtime check that could be forgotten."] # [doc = ""] # [doc = " ```"] # [doc = " use pn_interchange::Theory;"] # [doc = ""] # [doc = " let theory = Theory::parse(r#\"e = {0 => \"com.example\", 1 => [1, 4, uint], 2 => tstr}\"#)"] # [doc = "     .expect(\"an assignable theory\");"] # [doc = " let open = theory.open_companion();"] # [doc = " assert_eq!(open.floor(), (1, 4));"] # [doc = " assert!(open.to_cddl().contains(\"* (uint .gt 1) => any\"));"] # [doc = " ```"] # [derive (Clone , Debug)] pub struct OpenTheory { cddl : Cddl , table : RuleTable , patterns : BTreeMap < usize , XsdPattern > , label : NamespaceLabel , floor : (u64 , u64) , }

class_decisions.name: public-interchange
class_decisions.premises: Public canonical values, theories and registry data are recorded at their consuming boundaries. The Debug structural carrier preserves constructors, sequences, keys and literal contents as tagged JSON; lazy capabilities are described without advancing them. Canonical laws and iterator order remain binding inputs, never observation outputs.

class_decisions.name: public-documents
class_decisions.premises: Dataset input, template sources, projected values and rendered reports are public. The consuming document boundaries preserve available value structure; serde capability adapters inherit those boundaries without adding bounds or invoking deserializers twice.

class_decisions.name: public-execwrap
class_decisions.premises: Child arguments, configuration, outcomes and I/O are public. Tagged UTF-8/base64 preserves original bytes; relays write their original buffers. Read, Write and notification capabilities are not invoked for observation.

class_decisions.name: public-cli
class_decisions.premises: Control records, argv, public errors and serialized output are recorded at command boundaries. Parser and callback capabilities are described without an extra invocation. Non-string panic payloads have no introspection contract and are explicitly unavailable.

class_decisions.name: delivery
class_decisions.premises: The observer owns queue admission, timestamps, metric accounting, encoding, artifact publication and export. These bodies run under the labelled command operation and never recursively instrument observation. Public payload representation changes do not feed a binding return; delivery failures count loss. Artifact publication occurs only on the delivery worker. Full content is a capability selected by PN_OBSERVE_LEVEL=trace. Default span visits retain only command identity and outcome and never call payload Debug; command completion, WARN/ERROR, summaries and status remain emitted. Successful writes and whole-record loss are separately counted.

class_decisions.name: value-traits
class_decisions.premises: Hash, comparison, clone and teardown are structural plumbing inherited by the canonical coding and theory operations that consume the same value. The class inherits the complete set of declared interchange boundaries, including registry acquisition and its CDDL parsing. These bodies preserve their pre-observation implementation and introduce no fresh full-value record. Direct external consumers owe the same labelled caller boundary.

class_decisions.name: secret-carriers
class_decisions.premises: Protected carriers and export credentials expose only role and marker. No production ExposeSecret consumer is admitted. Adding a field, consumer or transport invalidates this body/type-bound admission.
